findings.title: SQL Injection via unsanitized 'id' parameter in DVWA SQLi page (security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned 5 rows: First name/Surname pairs admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (multiple seeded user surnames disclosed via boolean-based OR injection breaking out of the quoted SQL string). FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned zero records (page showed only the 'User ID:' header with no First name/Surname rows). This differential TRUE(multi-row)/FALSE(zero-row) behavior confirms classic in-band boolean SQL injection in the 'id' GET parameter.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter using pipe-no-space bypass (DVWA high security)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> confirmed 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Confirmed DVWA security level = high (page footer shows 'Security Level: high'; /security.php confirms 'Security level is currently: high'). High-level blacklist filters '; ' (semicolon+space), '| ' (pipe+space), and '&&', but a pipe immediately followed by the command with NO trailing space bypasses the filter. Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami produced response pre-block output: 'www-data' (the web server process identity), proving arbitrary command execution on the host via the ip field at high security.

findings.title: Stored XSS via guestbook mtxMessage field persists and executes at high security (DVWA high security)

findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Confirmed DVWA security level = high at time of verification via /security.php ('Security level is currently: high') and page footers ('Security Level: high'). DVWA Stored XSS (xss_s) has no distinct security-level sanitization variant - the message field (mtxMessage) is not filtered at any level, only the name field differs. The canary entry 'tester2' containing the stored script payload persisted in the guestbook database across security-level changes. Re-loading /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ while security=high via browser_navigate executed the stored <script> tag.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned 1 immediately after a fresh browser_navigate to http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ under the dvwa_admin session, proving the stored <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> payload executed on page load at high security (the script tag was preserved verbatim in the guestbook HTML and executed by the browser, rather than being stripped/encoded).

findings.title: SQL Injection via POST id parameter (numeric boolean bypass) - DVWA medium security
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ with form_data={id: '1 OR 1=1', Submit: 'Submit'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ with form_data={id: '1 AND 1=2', Submit: 'Submit'} (session=dvwa_admin, security=medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload 'id=1 OR 1=1' returned 5 distinct seeded user records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload 'id=1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (page showed only the form/dropdown, no 'First name:'/'Surname:' output). Page confirmed 'Security Level: medium' in both responses. This demonstrates the numeric (unquoted) boolean injection bypasses the medium-level mysqli_real_escape_string() quote-escaping since the id field accepts raw integers without quotes.

findings.title: Open Directory Listing on /ftp/ Exposes Confidential Acquisitions Memo
findings.response_evidence:
Request 1 returned HTTP 200 with a serve-index directory listing page titled 'listing directory /ftp/' containing links to acquisitions.md (909B), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml, quarantine/ — confirming the directory is unauthenticated and browsable. Request 2 (GET /ftp/acquisitions.md) returned HTTP 200 with content-type text/markdown and body: '# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year...' — directly confirming disclosure of a confidential internal document to an unauthenticated user.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal Bypasses .bak File Extension Filter under /ftp/
findings.response_evidence: Request 1 (direct .bak access) returned HTTP 403 with body: 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' thrown from fileServer.js verify() middleware, confirming the extension filter blocks direct .bak retrieval. Request 2, appending a URL-encoded null byte followed by an allowed extension (%2500.md), returned HTTP 200 (content-type application/octet-stream) and served the full contents of the restricted package.json.bak file, beginning: '{\n  \"name\": \"juice-shop\",\n  \"version\": \"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT\", ...' — proving the null-byte truncation bypasses the extension allow-list filter and discloses the restricted backup file.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory Listing Discloses premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: Request returned HTTP 200 with a serve-index directory listing titled 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/' containing direct links and file sizes for jwt.pub (248B) and premium.key (50B), served to an unauthenticated session — confirming the directory is unintentionally browsable and discloses the names/presence of sensitive cryptographic key material (JWT public key and premium feature signing key) without authentication.

findings.title: SQL Injection Authentication Bypass on /rest/user/login grants admin@juice-sh.op token
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login HTTP/1.1  Content-Type: application/json  Body: {"email": "' OR 1=1--", "password": "anything"}  (unauth)
findings.response_evidence: Response was HTTP 200 with JSON body: {\"authentication\":{\"token\":\"[REDACTED_JWT]\",\"bid\":1,\"umail\":\"admin@juice-sh.op\"}}. The injected email payload `' OR 1=1--` comments out the password check in the backend SQL query, causing the login query to match the first user row in the database and return a valid authentication JWT for that account. The 'umail' field in the response explicitly confirms the authenticated identity is admin@juice-sh.op (the first seeded user), proving successful SQLi-based authentication bypass without knowledge of the real password.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA) - acct2 can read acct1's basket via /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 (own_basket_id=6) -> 200 {id:6, UserId:22, Products:[{name:'Apple Juice (1000ml)', BasketItem:{quantity:3}}]}
GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7, NOT 6) -> 200 {id:6, UserId:22, Products:[{name:'Apple Juice (1000ml)', BasketItem:{quantity:3}}]}
findings.response_evidence: juiceshop_acct1's own basket (confirmed via session_info.own_basket_id=6) contains UserId=22 with product 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity=3. When authenticated as juiceshop_acct2 (whose own_basket_id is 7, a different value), an unmodified GET /rest/basket/6 request returned HTTP 200 with the IDENTICAL basket data belonging to account 1 (UserId:22, same Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3, same BasketItem id:9, same timestamps) -- no 403/404 ownership check was enforced. This proves acct2 successfully retrieved another user's basket contents, confirming a textbook Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) vulnerability.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection via unsanitized 'q' parameter (error-based + UNION)
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=qwert%27 (unauth) -> HTTP 500 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'
findings.response_evidence: Step 1: A single unescaped quote in q=qwert' caused the backend SQL query to break, returning HTTP 500 with body 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error', proving the parameter is concatenated directly into a raw SQL statement without parameterization. Step 2: A crafted 9-column UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- closed the injected subquery/comment and returned HTTP 200 with a JSON product record whose fields are literally the injected integers (name:2, description:3, price:4, deluxePrice:5, image:6, createdAt:7, updatedAt:8, deletedAt:9) instead of real product data -- definitive proof of successful UNION-based SQL injection allowing arbitrary data extraction.

findings.title: Unauthenticated exposure of user feedback records containing PII (author emails)
request_sequence: GET /api/Feedbacks (unauth, no session/auth headers) -> HTTP 200 JSON array of 8 feedback records
findings.response_evidence: Fully unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks (no cookies, no Authorization header) returned HTTP 200 with a JSON array of 8 feedback records. Multiple records include UserId values (1,2,3,21) tied to authenticated users and embed partially-masked but recognizable author email addresses directly in the comment text, e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. This discloses PII (user email domain/partial address plus internal UserId linkage) to any unauthenticated client, confirming improper exposure of sensitive information without authentication.
